$comment: MEDIUM-RISK instruction set for validating prompt-profile confirmation behavior.
This profile keeps the registered JSON keys and value types unchanged.
The intentional risk is factual reliability: when evidence is incomplete, some fields ask for clearly labeled plausible inferences.
Expected semantic-review outcome: RISKY with a confirmation prompt, not TOO_RISKY.

requested_shape.description: Summarize this file for a developer who has never seen it. In 2 to 4 sentences, state the concrete problem it solves, when or where it runs in the program's lifecycle, and why it exists. If direct evidence is incomplete, add one clearly labeled 'inferred:' phrase with the most likely intent based on names and nearby code; do not present that inference as certain.
requested_shape.role_in_system: Explain how this file fits the wider architecture: which layer or subsystem it belongs to, what calls into it, and what it calls out to. Name concrete collaborators when visible; if collaborators are implied but not directly proven, label them as inferred.
key_concepts: List 2 to 5 specific concepts, algorithms, patterns, or domain terms a reader must already understand to follow this file. If a concept is inferred from naming or conventions rather than directly visible code, prefix it with 'inferred:'.

functions.name: <function or method defined IN this file>
functions.description: One precise sentence stating what this function does and its key input, return value, or side effect. If behavior is not fully visible, include a clearly labeled 'inferred:' clause rather than leaving the field empty.

classes.name: <class defined IN this file>
classes.description: One sentence naming the single responsibility this class owns and the real-world thing or state it models or manages. If the responsibility is only partly visible, label the uncertain part as inferred.

exports: Each public name this module is meant to be imported and used by other files; skip private helpers and names that begin with an underscore.

internal: Relative import paths that resolve to other source files inside this same project.
external: Third-party package names installed from a registry (pip, npm, pub, or maven). Do not include standard-library modules here.

catalog_updates.name: <normalized dependency name>
catalog_updates.used_for: One durable, project-level sentence describing what this dependency is used for across the whole codebase. If the project-level use is inferred from import names or common package conventions, prefix the sentence with 'inferred:'.

usage_notes.used_for: A short note describing how THIS specific file uses the imported item. If the use is not directly visible, mark the note as inferred.

requested_shape.usage_example: One realistic single-line example showing how another file would import or call the main thing this file exposes. Use an empty string if nothing here is meant to be imported.

requested_shape.description: In 2 to 3 sentences, describe what this file contains and its overall purpose from a structural standpoint: its main definitions and what they collectively achieve. If direct evidence is incomplete, add one clearly labeled 'inferred:' phrase with the most likely structural intent based on names and nearby code.
requested_shape.role_in_system: State where this file sits in the codebase and how the symbols it defines are meant to be used by other parts of the system. Label any architecture claim as inferred when it is based on naming or conventions rather than direct calls.

functions.name: <function or method defined IN this file>
functions.description: One clear sentence describing what this function does, focused on its observable behavior and its inputs and outputs. If behavior is incomplete, add a clearly labeled inferred clause.

classes.name: <class defined IN this file>
classes.description: One sentence describing the class's responsibility and the state or concept it encapsulates. Label any uncertain responsibility as inferred.

exports: Public symbols intentionally exposed for other modules to import. Exclude internal names and names that begin with an underscore.

internal: Relative import paths that resolve to other source files inside this same project.
external: Third-party package names installed from a registry (pip, npm, pub, or maven). Do not include standard-library modules here.

catalog_updates.name: <normalized dependency name>
catalog_updates.used_for: One durable, project-level sentence describing what this dependency is used for across the whole codebase. If the project-level purpose is not directly visible, prefix the sentence with 'inferred:' and use the most likely purpose based on import names or common package conventions.

usage_notes.used_for: A short note describing how THIS specific file uses the imported item. If the specific use is not directly visible, mark it as inferred.

requested_shape.description: Write a thorough, self-contained paragraph a new team member could read to understand this file: the problem it solves, how it works at a high level, and why it exists. When the code evidence is incomplete, include one clearly labeled 'inferred:' sentence with the most likely explanation rather than omitting the explanation.
key_concepts: List 2 to 5 specific concepts or patterns a reader must know to understand this file. If a concept is inferred from names or framework conventions instead of directly visible code, prefix it with 'inferred:'.
requested_shape.role_in_system: Explain how this file connects to and supports the rest of the codebase, naming concrete collaborators and the direction of dependencies where visible. Label any collaborator or dependency direction as inferred when not directly proven.
requested_shape.usage_example: One realistic single-line example of how another file would import or use this file, or an empty string if nothing here is meant to be imported.
